name: Fractile
description: Fractile is privately held and has no ticker. Review its funding rounds, its investors, and the points to confirm before buying or selling.
ledes: Fractile is a privately held semiconductor company. Its shares are not listed on an exchange and have no quoted market price; the principal public reference points are the financing rounds in which the company has raised capital. Its most recent reported financing was a $720 million Series C round, which the UK government, one of the round's investors, confirmed on November 11, 2026.

Founded in 2022 and based in London, Fractile designs chips for running artificial intelligence models, together with the software and machine learning research that support them. Existing shares change hands in privately negotiated transactions and remain subject to the company's transfer restrictions.
table_note: Fractile has not disclosed the valuation of any round. It did not announce its Series C; the amount shown is as reported by TechCrunch on November 11, 2026, and the valuation as reported by the Financial Times and Reuters.
round_notes: The UK government invested in the Series C through its Sovereign AI Venture Fund, alongside the British Business Bank. Fractile's chief executive has said the round will fund delivery of the company's first chips and systems in 2027.

A round valuation reflects the terms of the preferred stock issued in that round. Most shares sold by employees are common stock, which carries fewer rights and typically trades at a discount to the preferred price.
investors: Thrive Capital, Founders Fund, Lightspeed Venture Partners and Redpoint led the Series C, in which CapitalG also invested. Accel, Factorial Funds and Founders Fund co-led the Series B, and Kindred Capital, the NATO Innovation Fund and Oxford Science Enterprises led the seed round. Other investors include Conviction, Felicis, 8VC and Inovia Capital.
spv_sentence: No special purpose vehicles naming Fractile appear in SEC Form D filings.
sources: Sources: Fractile's Series B announcement; the UK government's announcement dated November 11, 2026; reports by TechCrunch (November 2026), the Financial Times and Reuters (November 2026), SiliconANGLE (May 2026) and Tech.eu (July 2024); and SEC Form D filings.
